That's bizarre, I've never heard of a credit card company charging back payments that low. Almost every single card issuer of a major brand (Visa, MC, AMEX, Discover) uses a "minimum chargeback" threshold on the amount per transaction, and will write off anything below that threshold without actually submitting a chargeback. They do this because the issuer also has to pay a certain amount per transaction charged back, and it doesn't make sense for them to chargeback $1 transactions at a cost of roughly $10 per transaction (this amount varies greatly, but usually is not much less than $10 per chargeback).

I don't sell a lot of products online so I can't offer an alternative, but that is highly unusual you would receive chargebacks like that. If you haven't already, I would contact paypal and let them know this appears to be malicious abuse of chargebacks, and you will no longer use their services if they can't protect you from something like this.
